answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake bond before it can trade, like a toll on a ridge road: one identity costs one bond, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. The bond is slashed if the agent cheats, so the cost of an attack ripples beyond the single fake identity to the attacker's whole stake. Verified agents graduate to a shared jetty where only bonded, good-standing agents can dock and transact, and the bond makes fake fleets unprofitable before they ever set sail.
